entry.title: T2K with gadolinium
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. T2K reports updated oscillation parameters using 21.4 (16.3) x 10^20 protons on target in neutrino (antineutrino) mode, including 1.7 x 10^20 more neutrino-mode POT than the previous result. For the first time the sample includes data taken with gadolinium-doped Super-Kamiokande. The far-detector selection and the systematic error treatment were improved, and both the semi-frequentist and the Bayesian analyses favour normal mass ordering.

entry.title: PIKACHU Phase 1
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. PIKACHU searches at Kamioka for two-neutrino double-beta decay of 160Gd using Ce:GAGG scintillators. The new paper characterises the backgrounds through delayed-coincidence analysis and GEANT4-based spectral fits. Surface contamination of the crystal, identified from the distortion of the 214Po alpha spectrum, led to an improved background model. No significant excess from 160Gd decay was observed.

entry.title: NuDEx reconstruction study
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. NuDEx plans a search for neutrinoless double-beta decay of 82Se with a high-pressure SeF6 negative-ion time projection chamber. A simulation study compares FFT deconvolution with direct waveform fitting for reconstructing the longitudinal coordinate from the arrival-time separation of SeF5- and SeF6-. On 855 events common to both methods, the separation RMSEs were 0.180 ms (direct fit) and 0.222 ms (FFT).

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper computes the contribution of the Δ-direct-Urca process to neutrino emissivity in neutron stars containing Δ isobars, which the authors say had not been evaluated explicitly. It matters for neutron-star cooling, where nucleonic and hyperonic Urca processes are the dominant neutrino-emitting channels.

entry.title: The authors revisit the published 7Be K-capture measurement of the 7Li recoil peak by Smolsky et al
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors revisit the published 7Be K-capture measurement of the 7Li recoil peak by Smolsky et al. They use its measured width (FWHM = 6.7 eV, sigma_E = 2.9 eV) to determine the spatial extent of the neutrino wave packet. This gives a direct experimental handle on a quantity usually treated only theoretically.

entry.title: The paper proves that every completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations of the ma
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves that every completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane is blind to a Majorana phase in two-flavour oscillations. A rate anisotropy in the environment can supply a phase reference, and the paper gives the resulting time dependence. It states when decoherence can and cannot make a Majorana phase visible in oscillations.

entry.title: The authors give semianalytic approximations for the outcome of slow and fast flavour conversion in quasihomog
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors give semianalytic approximations for the outcome of slow and fast flavour conversion in quasihomogeneous neutrino ensembles. They report good agreement with multiangle and multienergy solutions of the kinetic equations, independent of mass ordering. Such prescriptions can serve as subgrid schemes in supernova simulations that cannot include neutrino quantum kinetics.

entry.title: The paper studies how well kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could measure the primary cosmic-r
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper studies how well kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could measure the primary cosmic-ray spectrum from the atmospheric neutrino flux. It finds that different cosmic-ray models can be distinguished with high statistical significance, including uncertainties in neutrino cross sections and hadronic interactions. The result turns the atmospheric neutrino sample into a full-sky, long-term cosmic-ray monitor.

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors study an su(n) Hamiltonian with one- and two-body terms, which describes collective neutrino oscillations among other systems. By truncating the BBGKY hierarchy they obtain a systematic way to go beyond mean field, with polynomial scaling on a classical computer.
